children: Electra Therapeutics filed a 424B4 prospectus for its initial public offering on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ETRA. The company is offering 23,333,334 shares at $15.00 per share, for gross proceeds of approximately $350.0 million (about $319.9 million net). Jefferies, TD Cowen, Evercore ISI and Cantor are acting as joint bookrunners, and Electra qualifies as an emerging growth company.

Electra Therapeutics is a late clinical‑stage biopharmaceutical company developing precision medicines that selectively remove disease‑driving immune cells by targeting signal regulatory proteins (SIRP). Its lead candidate, ipsoprubart, is a pan‑SIRP monoclonal antibody engineered to deplete pathogenic myeloid cells and T cells through ADCC/ADCP while preserving normal immune function. Ipsoprubart is in a global Phase 2/3 registrational program for secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) and has received FDA Breakthrough Therapy and EMA PRIME designations. In a Phase 1b study, frontline malignancy‑associated HLH patients achieved 100% 8‑week overall survival and 100% overall response with rapid biomarker improvements.

Beyond sHLH, Electra is studying ipsoprubart in relapsed/refractory T/NK cell malignancies following encouraging tumor responses seen in early clinical experience. The company’s second program, ELA822, is a SIRPγ‑specific monoclonal antibody designed to selectively deplete activated T cells for chronic immune and inflammatory diseases. ELA822 began a Phase 1 study in healthy volunteers in Europe, with plans to initiate a Phase 1/2 study in patients with T cell‑mediated disorders. Electra operates a capital‑efficient model, outsourcing manufacturing to experienced CMOs and focusing resources on development and regulatory execution.
: U.S. diagnosed sHLH population of ~12,600 in 2025, potentially rising to ~17,500 by 2028 as awareness and diagnosis improve.
: sHLH diagnoses grew at an estimated 11.5% CAGR from 2021 to 2025; growing use of immune‑effector therapies is expanding related HLH‑like syndromes.
: Electra is, to its knowledge, the first to advance SIRP‑targeted precision immune cell depletion into clinical development, with FDA Breakthrough Therapy and EMA PRIME designations.
: Off‑label regimens (corticosteroids, etoposide, alemtuzumab, ruxolitinib, tocilizumab, anakinra); emapalumab approved for primary HLH and MAS in Still’s disease (not sHLH broadly).
: Rising use of CAR‑T and bispecifics (IEC‑HS cases), improving diagnostic frameworks (e.g., OHI index), and growing recognition of hyperinflammatory syndromes.
: Headquarters in South San Francisco, California
: Clinical operations across the United States and Europe
: Multiple contract manufacturing organizations; Breakthrough Therapy (FDA) and PRIME (EMA) regulatory engagement
: SURPASS Phase 2/3 registrational trial and COMPASS natural history study in sHLH; Phase 1 trial in T/NK cell malignancies; Phase 1 HV trial for ELA822 in Europe
: Cash runway into 2029 with IPO proceeds, subject to operating plan
, President & Chief Executive Officer - Former COO at Star Therapeutics; commercialization roles at True North/Sanofi and Gilead; Pharm.D. and M.B.A. from University of New Mexico.
, Chief Medical Officer - Board‑certified hematologist and clinician‑scientist; prior clinical development leadership at Astex Pharmaceuticals.
, Chief Scientific Officer - Extensive translational R&D leadership across immunology and oncology; former EVP Translational Sciences at Star Therapeutics.
, Chief Technical Officer - 30+ years in biologics CMC; led scale‑up and quality functions at multiple biopharma companies including Aravive and Star Therapeutics.
, Chief Financial Officer - Two decades in biopharma capital markets; former Portfolio Manager at RS Investments.
, Chairperson of the Board - Biotech company builder and executive; CEO of Neuron23; former CEO of True North, iPierian and CytomX.
: Jefferies; TD Cowen; Evercore ISI; Cantor

: Advance ipsoprubart in sHLH through Phase 2/3 topline and BLA readiness; advance ipsoprubart in T/NK cell malignancies; advance ELA822 through Phase 1 and initiate Phase 1/2; other R&D, capex, working capital and general corporate purposes.
